summary: Barry County, MO: a 100-foot steel fire tower finished in 1955 on land bought in 1944; the record lists it gone and no source found dates the removal.

facts.design: 100-foot steel fire tower with a small cabin at the top, finished in 1955 to replace a wartime pole-type or wooden tower
facts.status_note: The record lists the tower as gone. No source I found dates its removal or describes the towersite today.
facts.agency: Missouri Conservation Commission, later the Missouri Department of Conservation

events.note: Missouri Conservation Commission buys a 40-acre towersite four miles west of Washburn (Pineville Democrat, September 7, 1944)
100-foot steel tower completed in September 1955 (Neosho News) to replace a temporary pole-type (wooden) tower from the war years
Bobby Lawrence, transferred from the Joplin tower, named to man the new tower (Neosho News, September 1955)
Old tower residence dismantled and a new building constructed (FY 1956-57 report)
April 2, 1961 grass fire pushed by a strong wind; Wayne Lawrence, 50, found dead; his brother Bob was an observer at the tower (Jefferson City Post-Tribune)

notes_for_editor: The compiled Central US Lookouts page carries the newspaper and annual-report extracts (Pineville Democrat, Neosho News, Jefferson City Post-Tribune, Springfield News-Leader); the originals were not reached. The record's gone status has no dated source on the page. Lead, not cited: a RootsWeb Washburn history page (sites.rootsweb.com/~mobarry/Washburn/index.htm) turned up in search with photo captions dated 1992 about taking the tower down; fetch_text returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited. Worth checking by hand for the removal date and owner. Height conflict: the September 1955 Neosho News item says 100 feet, the 1990 Springfield News-Leader article says 1,000 feet; the story uses 100 feet. Bobby (1955, Neosho News) and Bob (1961, 1990) Lawrence are probably the same man; the sources do not say so. The Missouri Life article was blocked (HTTP 403).
